subject: Engelska 5
title: False friends and typical Swedish mistakes
sourceSummary: Words that look Swedish but mean something completely different, plus word pairs that Swedish merges into one — lend/borrow, teach/learn, fun/funny.

questions.opener: The word looks like a Swedish word — but means something completely different.
questions.explanation: "Eventually" means till slut, så småningom (in the end, eventually). The Swedish word "eventuellt" is "possibly" or "perhaps" in English. The mistake changes the meaning completely.

questions.prompt: Your friend asks if you're coming. You mean "eventuellt". What should you say?
questions.opener: If you say "eventually" you're actually promising something completely different.
questions.explanation: "I might come" expresses uncertainty. "I will eventually come" means you will definitely come — but only later, which is a promise you might not want to make.

questions.opener: Closely related to a Swedish word — but it isn't the building.
questions.explanation: "Fabric" means tyg (cloth). The Swedish word "fabrik" is "factory" in English.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "Could you ___ me your charger until tomorrow?"
questions.opener: The Swedish word "låna" covers both directions — English has two different words.
questions.explanation: "Lend" is to give something out on loan, "borrow" is to receive something on loan. You're asking the person to lend to you, so "lend" is correct. Alternatively: "Could I borrow your charger?"

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "My grandmother ___ me how to bake bread."
questions.opener: Who is passing the knowledge on to whom?
questions.explanation: "Teach" is to pass knowledge on, "learn" is to acquire it yourself. The Swedish word "lära" is used both ways, which leads to the mistake "she learned me".

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: "The party was really ___ — I enjoyed every minute."
questions.opener: Is it about having a good time, or about laughing?
questions.explanation: "Fun" describes something enjoyable. "Funny" means comical or amusing in a laughter-inducing way — and can also mean strange: "That's funny, the door was open."

questions.prompt: Correct the four errors: "I will eventually join you later. My brother learned me to drive, and he borrowed me his car. Actually, I work at a fabric."
questions.opener: Four words look right to a Swedish eye but mean something else.
questions.answer: I might join you later. My brother taught me to drive, and he lent me his car. Actually, I work at a factory.
steps: "eventually" → "might". The writer means "eventuellt" (i.e. uncertainty), not "till slut" (in the end).
"learned me" → "taught me". The brother was the one passing on the skill, so it's "teach" in the past tense: "taught".
"borrowed me his car" → "lent me his car". He gave the car out on loan; "borrow" means to receive something on loan.
"a fabric" → "a factory". "Fabric" means cloth. Note that "Actually" is in fact used correctly here — it means "faktiskt" (indeed), which is what the sentence needs.

questions.prompt: List the most common false friends between Swedish and English.
questions.opener: Words that look familiar but mean something else.
questions.answer: eventually = till slut (eventuellt = possibly) · actually = faktiskt (aktuellt = current) · fabric = tyg (fabrik = factory) · gift = present (gift = married/poison) · sensible = förnuftig (sensibel = sensitive) · control = styra (kontrollera = check) · blank = tom (blank = shiny) · novel = roman (novell = short story) · recipe = recept på mat (recept från läkare = prescription)
